text:
Neurologist 
Emergency Department

11 February, 2018

Dear Doctor, 

Re: Ms Maria Joseph, aged 39

Thank you for seeing Ms Joseph who requires an urgent assessment and treatment for a persistent headache and possible neurological damage following a fall at home today. 

Ms Joseph, with no known past illnesses, has been suffering from a persistent headache over the past five days. Initially, given no significant neurological symptoms presented, the cause of her headache was thought to be exercise tension or personal dilemma related, so she was advised to rest, and treated with 500g of Paracetamol four hourly. 

Four days later, Ms Joseph’s headache was exacerbated radiating from her frontal head to the left side, with throbbing sensation, blurred vision and frequent vomiting. At this stage, a severe migraine was suspected, and she was treated with Pethidine 100mg and Maxolon 10 mg stat. 

Ms Joseph’s persistent headache was led to a fall at home today. As a result, she has sustained an injury to her right arm with bruises on her left leg. She is also semi-conscious with slurred speech, tachycardia and slightly elevated blood pressure. 

As Ms Joseph’s symptoms indicate a possibility of intracranial pathology, she will require an urgent assessment and management under your care.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

RN
(203 W)
